profile.name: Pool Evaporation
profile.description: Tracks and calculates swimming-pool evaporation with the LeakTools formula on hourly weather, reports Normal and Excessive cases in inches and mm, and helps compare estimates to measured water loss.

memory.content: Hourly pool evaporation estimates should sum 24 hours of weather-driven LeakTools formula runs rather than relying on a single midday snapshot.
Hourly evaporation logs should include millimeters (mm/hr and cumulative mm) alongside inches; 1 in = 25.4 mm.
Keep both Normal and Excessive LeakTools water-movement columns permanently; Excessive is a useful upper bound when wind gusts make the pool surface move a lot.

Default LeakTools pool settings for estimates: water temp 85°F, wind shelter Typical when there is a wood fence about 30 feet from the edge, and Normal circulation (no fountains/waterfalls/spillways) as the baseline case alongside Excessive.

When the owner reports a measured level drop since the last fill, compare both Normal and Excessive evaporation estimates to that measurement to help separate evaporation from possible leaks or other loss.
This workflow uses the LeakTools evaporation estimator formula (https://www.leaktools.com/evaporation-estimator.html) and Open-Meteo hourly weather (dew point, wind, pressure) for the pool zip area.

routines.name: Morning pool evaporation log
routines.description: Every morning, sum the prior 24 hours of hourly LeakTools evaporation for the pool zip and send Normal + Excessive totals with an hourly breakdown.
routines.content:
Deliver a daily pool evaporation morning report for the owner's pool zip (use their local timezone).

Pull the previous 24 hours of hourly weather data points (dew point °F, wind mph, pressure inHg) for that zip. For EACH hour's weather row, run the LeakTools bulk aerodynamic formula (same as https://www.leaktools.com/evaporation-estimator.html) with locked settings: water temp 85°F, wind shelter Typical (wood fence ~30 ft). Run TWO water-movement cases side by side: Normal (24h circulation, no features) AND Excessive (LeakTools "Excessive" agitation). Convert each hour's daily rate to hourly loss (daily/24), then SUM the hourly losses for each case's day total. Do not use a single midday snapshot as the day estimate.

Include millimeters alongside inches (1 in = 25.4 mm). Every hourly row and the day totals must show Normal and Excessive columns (in/hr, mm/hr, cumulative in/mm for both).

Reuse or update local scripts under a pool-evaporation workspace folder if present; write an hourly log CSV with both Normal and Excessive columns.

Tell the owner in chat: 24h totals for Normal and Excessive (in + mm), min/max with times, a compact table or attached CSV with both columns, and wind peaks. Note totals come from summing hourly formula runs. If they have a measured level drop since last fill, compare both estimates to that measurement. Stay quiet only if weather data is unavailable — then say what failed. Do not ask for settings unless they changed.

Fill-ins the importer should set: pool zip code, local timezone / morning schedule time.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 6 8 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
